newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Ex-Cyprus foreign minister Iakovou seeks presidency.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Cyprus foreign minister Iakovou seeks presidency.

text.p: Former Cyprus foreign minister George Iakovou announced on Wednesday that he would stand as an independent in presidential elections on the eastern Mediterranean island scheduled for early 1998.

"My aspiration is a peaceful, federal solution to the Cyprus problem which will serve the interests of the Cyprus people independently of national or religious orientations," he told a news conference.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded its northern third in 1974 in response to a brief coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Iakovou, 59, was foreign minister in the centre-right government of Spyros Kyprianou and the centre-left government of George Vassiliou from 1983 to 1993.
During his term Cyprus applied in July 1990 for European Union membership. Entry talks start next year.
Iakovou said his administration would try to reverse an economic slowdown.

GDP growth registered a 1.9 percent rise in 1996, from an estimated growth rate of 6.0 percent in 1995. Authorities have blamed external factors and a 7.0 percent contraction in tourism arrivals -- a fifth of GDP.

"The economic slowdown Cyprus faces today has to be intercepted. Emphasis will be put on upgrading the development of the economy ... A robust economy is a prerequisite for our acceptance in the European Union," Iakovou said.
His bid is likely to get support from Communist Akel, the second-largest party.

Presidential elections are due before the end of February. Right-wing incumbent President Glafcos Clerides, elected for a five-year term in February 1993, has said he would decide in the autumn whether to stand again.
